title: Introduce values sanitizer + ordered init hook sequence for private Helm charts
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Private deployments have grown a variety of edge configurations (tolerations, nodeAffinity snippets, CRD toggles, and bootstrap ordering). During several upgrade incidents we observed non-deterministic init-job races and invalid values being passed through the private installer values which led to failed upgrades (SUP-1287). This PR introduces a Helm-side values sanitizer, a small templating helper library, and an ordered init-hook sequence with explicit lock semantics to reduce upgrade failures and make chart behavior more deterministic.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a values sanitizer (helm/_helpers/values_sanitizer.tpl) that normalizes and validates common private-only fields (cidr blocks, service CIDR overlays, boolean toggles, CRD install flags, and legacy top-level keys). Sanitizer errors are surfaced as helm template-time warnings and (optionally) hard errors when --set enforceValidation=true.
- Introduces templating helpers for affinity/toleration fragments to avoid repetition and inconsistent merges across charts.
- Replaces ad-hoc init jobs with an ordered init-hook sequence (init/01-bootstrap-cert, init/02-migrate-config, init/03-leader-lock) that uses a lightweight ConfigMap-based leader lock to serialize migration steps during upgrades. Init jobs are annotated with hook-weight to guarantee order across Helm releases.
- Adds a new values key private.installation.enforceValidation (default: false) and private.installation.initOrdering.enabled (default: true).
- Adds preStop hooks and explicit terminationGracePeriodSeconds to stateful components touched by init jobs to improve graceful shutdown during rollbacks.
- Adds documentation examples and a new test harness in tests/helm/priv-installer-sanity.sh that runs helm template + kubeval against a matrix of values.

Checklist: 
- [x] values sanitizer implementation and docs examples
- [x] ordered init hooks with leader lock
- [x] templating helpers for affinity/tolerations
- [x] e2e template/kubeval test script
- [x] CHANGELOG/release notes entry
- [x] feature flag gating (enforceValidation & initOrdering)

Links: K8s best-practices: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/container-lifecycle-hooks/; Incident SUP-1287 notes: internal/incident/SUP-1287

Notes on behavior and upgrade safety: 
- The leader-lock used by init hooks is a namespaced ConfigMap keyed by release name; the lock is acquired with a short backoff and 5m TTL. If lock acquisition fails the hook will retry; during a rollback the ordering prevents simultaneous migrations.
- When enforceValidation is enabled, helm template will fail early for common misconfigurations (overlapping CIDRs, malformed CIDR, invalid boolean types provided as strings). We intentionally keep the default off to avoid breaking existing automated installs; this is intended for customers to opt into during dry-run validation and later CI gates.
- Templating helpers attempt to preserve user-provided blocks when present; they only inject defaults when keys are missing. This reduces surprise for operators with bespoke affinity settings.

Testing performed: 
- Unit: helm template + kubeval against 4 value matrices (default, custom-affinity, enforceValidation-on with invalid-cidr, private CRDs disabled).
- Integration: ran installer in a local KinD cluster and exercised upgrade/rollback path with 2 sequential releases.
- Load: smoke test on Dedicated staging cluster to validate init-job serialization under load.

Migration and rollout guidance for customers: 
1) Run helm template with enforceValidation=true in staging to catch value issues.
2) If any enforceValidation checks fail, fix values or explicitly set the legacy keys mapping in values.yaml.
3) Enable initOrdering (default true) for upgrades; rollback should be safe since the init hooks are idempotent and ordered.

Release notes: see release_notes field.

review_conversation: 2026-03-01 Miguel Santos: Left a few nits on helper naming and suggested making the lock TTL configurable via values. Also requested a brief note about why we chose ConfigMap vs Lease API.

2026-03-01 Asha Kapoor: Reply: made TTL configurable (private.installation.lockTTL) and added note in docs explaining Lease vs ConfigMap tradeoffs; Lease felt heavier for air-gapped clusters without coordination permission. Marked Miguel's comments as addressed.

2026-03-02 Priya Nair: Comment: enforceValidation=false default is safe, but we should add a short migration note in the release notes so operators don't flip it blindly. Also asked for a kubeval step in CI.
2026-03-02 Asha Kapoor: Reply: added release notes and CI kubeval job in pipeline (see CI checks).
2026-03-03 Kenji Watanabe: Approve after verifying ordered hook weights and confirming idempotency of migration job.
merge_details: Squash merge by Asha Kapoor. Commit message: 'helm(private-installer): add values sanitizer and ordered init hooks; docs, tests, helpers'
release_notes: Private installer: added values sanitizer (opt-in enforcement), templating helpers for affinity/tolerations, and an ordered init-hook sequence with ConfigMap-based leader lock to reduce upgrade/rollback races. Default behavior unchanged; operators should run helm template --set private.installation.enforceValidation=true in staging to validate values before enabling in production.
notes_for_maintainers: Watch for any customer reports about template-time warnings after this release; we intentionally emit warnings for deprecated top-level keys — follow docs to migrate. If customers run into lock acquisition failures in heavy upgrade windows, increase private.installation.lockTTL or disable initOrdering temporarily.
special_instructions: When backporting to release branches, ensure values.schema.json changes are included to avoid template-time mismatches. Do not enable enforceValidation by default on patch backports.
